compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090M Blackwell, 82 SMs, 128KB shmem/SM, 896GB/s. Tensor cores not directly accessible in HLSL cs_6_8 (no WMMA in DXIL standard); rely on FMA. Window N=16, C=32, H=4 hidden=128. Tiny matmuls per window; ~57600 windows.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Per-window working set tiny: x[16,32]=1KB fp16, qkv weights 96*32=6KB, proj 32*32=2KB, fc1 128*32=8KB, fc2 32*128=8KB, plus norms/bias/rpe. Total ~26KB weights -> fits easily in shared memory shared across whole threadgroup. Each window has N=16 tokens, 32 channels. Full fusion per window is highly feasible.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: HLSL lacks tensor core intrinsics in cs_6_8 directly; must use scalar/vector FMA. Compute is modest (mem-bound regime likely).

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input 29.49M fp16 = 59MB read + 59MB write. Weights tiny and reusable. Bandwidth-bound on activation I/O. Goal: read x once, write out once, do all compute fused.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Naive multi-pass would multiply BW use. Full fusion is essential.

register_pressure.notes: Per-window: 16 tokens * 32 ch fp16 = 512 fp16 values. With 64 threads/block, ~8 fp16/thread for x. Hidden 16*128=2048 fp16 -> 32/thread. Manageable.
register_pressure.risk: Hidden activations may need shared memory rather than registers; 128KB shmem/SM ample.

nodes.notes: PROBLEM: Simplified Swin block on (1,720,1280,32) fp16 with window_size=4x4, single head, no shift. PHASES per window: (1) LN1, (2) QKV linear (32->96), (3) attention 16x16 with rpe bias + softmax, (4) attn@V, (5) proj (32->32), (6) residual, (7) LN2, (8) fc1 (32->128), (9) GELU, (10) fc2 (128->32), (11) residual. WINDOWS: 720/4 * 1280/4 = 180*320 = 57600 independent windows. CANONICAL: each window independent -> map 1 window per threadgroup. WORKING SET per window fits in registers+shmem (weights ~26KB shared across all groups; activations per window: x[16,32]=1KB, qkv[16,96]=3KB, attn[16,16]=512B, fc1_out[16,128]=4KB). FULL FUSION FEASIBLE -> single kernel, read input once, write output once. BOTTLENECK REGIMES: (a) memory-bound on activation streaming (most likely given 896GB/s and ~120MB I/O => ~0.13ms floor); (b) compute-bound if many redundant matmul ops not coalesced; (c) sync-bound if too many barriers across tiny reductions. KNOBS: threads per group (32/64/128), reuse pattern for weights (constant cache vs groupshared preload), accumulation precision (fp32 for LN/softmax stability), layout of activations in groupshared, vectorized loads (float4 of fp16 = 8 elements via uint4 pack). FAMILY A (PRIMARY): single-kernel per-window full fusion, weights in groupshared (loaded by all groups identically) or just read from buffer with L1/L2 cache. FAMILY B: split into 2 kernels (attention + MLP) — abandoned due to extra global RT. FAMILY C: per-token threadgroup (smaller) — worse since attention needs cross-token within window. SELECT A. SELF_CHECK: families differ on fusion granularity; cannot be combined.

action.description: Implement a single fused HLSL compute shader where each threadgroup processes one 4x4 window (16 tokens, 32 channels). Use 32 threads/group (one per token mapped via warp), with fp32 accumulation for LN/softmax. Stage activations in groupshared memory; read weights directly from SRV (relies on L1/L2 reuse across the 57600 groups). Dispatch (nW*nH, 1, 1) = (57600,1,1). Compute LN1 -> QKV -> attn(softmax+rpe) -> AV -> proj -> +res -> LN2 -> fc1 -> GELU -> fc2 -> +res -> store.
action.rationale: Establishes correctness-first fully fused baseline. Memory traffic minimized to one read+one write of activations. Per-window math is tiny so register pressure is fine.
action.title: Full single-kernel fusion: LN+W-MSA+MLP per window, one global read/write

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin transformer block (LN, W-MSA with rpe, MLP) over a (1,720,1280,32) fp16 tensor with 4x4 windows and single head. 57600 independent windows, each with tiny per-window math (N=16 tokens, C=32, hidden=128). All weights total ~26KB and easily fit in groupshared/L2. The kernel is memory-bandwidth bound: minimizing global I/O via full fusion (single read of input, single write of output) is the dominant optimization. Stable accumulation in fp32 for LayerNorm and softmax is required for the rtol=0.01/atol=0.01 tolerance.
open_questions: Does HLSL cs_6_8 on this driver reliably support native float16_t arithmetic and 16-bit Buffer typed loads, or must we use ByteAddressBuffer with packing?
What is the input memory layout in practice: is the (B,H,W,C) buffer truly C-innermost contiguous, ensuring coalesced fp16 loads per token?
Best threadgroup size: 32 (1 warp/window) vs 64 vs 128 (multi-window) — which minimizes latency on RTX5090M?
Should weights be preloaded to groupshared or rely on L2? With 57600 groups but small weights, L2 likely caches all weights effectively.
Can we exploit DP4a/WMMA-like paths via DXIL extensions in cs_6_8, or are we limited to scalar/vector FMA?
What precision is acceptable in attention softmax — fp16 accumulation likely violates tolerance; needs fp32.
Does the GELU approximation choice (tanh vs erf) matter within tolerance vs PyTorch nn.GELU default?
Are there alignment requirements for vectorized loads given the window stride (W*C=1280*32=40960 elements per row)?
